text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- George Moeller, president of the Amsterdam Exchanges, calls for increased supervision of individuals active in the investment world. (p1)
- Harsh 1995/1996 winter and cold weather at the end of last year pushes 1996 sales of natural gas monopoly distributor Gasunie to a record. (p1)
- Consumers spending on food rises 10 pct in October, largest turnover growth in ten years. (p1)
- Insurer Zwolsche Algemene, a U.S. ITT Hartford unit, boosts 1996 net to Dfl 70 million. (p3)
- Publisher Wegener Arcade to sell TV station TV 10. (p3)
- Cargo traffic in the port of Amsterdam rises 19 pct to 37 million tonnes in 1996. (p3)
- Dutch businesses seize commercial opportunities of the 200 kilometre Elfstedentocht ice-skating race on the lakes between 11 Friesian towns on Saturday. (p4)
- Local authorities bank BNG books five percent higher 1996 earnings at Dfl 317 million.
VOLKSKRANT
- Province of Friesland is expecting an invasion of people to watch traditional ice-skating race. (p1)
- Belgian PM Jean-Luc Dehaene criticises French president Jacques Chirac for his "aggressive" attitude towards Dutch drugs policy. (p1)
- Entrepreneur Wichard de Waard, who wants to take over bankrupt aircraft maker Fokker, already has support of Philips Electronics founder Frits Philips. (p2)
- Regional utility company Reger to be sold by tender. (p2)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Food retailer Schuitema's 1996 turnover rises 3.7 pct to 4.1 billion guilders. (p21)
- Dry cleaners' group Palthe again achieves a profit in 1996 and reports takeover of two Belgian rivals. (p21)
- Financial chief of Travel Unie, Rene Krijt, forced to leave company. (p23)
- National Investment bank (NIB) had better 1996 than originally expected. (p23)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Amsterdam zoo Artis gets its penguins inside to protect them from the cold. (p1)
- Sugar producer CSM books 1995/1996 net up from Dfl 186.5 to Dfl 201.6 million. (p13)
TROUW
- Entertainment group Endemol and broadcaster RTL get more than half a million guilders from Foster Parents plan to make a programme about the organisation. (p9)
